title: architecture-review-kv-cache-prefetch-routing-followup-2026-08-10
content:
Architecture review follow-up notes - KV cache prefetch & routing (RFC review)

Date: 2026-08-10
Attendees: Liam Chen (owner), Aisha Patel, Marcos Rivera, Elena Ivanova, Priya Singh, Jordan Miles (observability)
Meeting purpose: Capture decisions and concrete next steps after the June RFC + July perf experiments. Focus areas: prefetch heuristics, routing policy integration (latency vs cost tiers), correctness and multi-tenant isolation, rollout plan.

Summary / decisions made
- Prefetch trigger: adopt hybrid heuristic (prefix-frequency + recent-hot-window). We will use a frequency-based score (weighted 70%) and a recency signal (30%) to decide prefetch candidates. Threshold tunable via config per-customer.
- Routing integration: prefetch-aware routing flags will be exposed to the routing policy. When a request includes a prefetch ticket, routing will prefer nodes with matching KV-shard locality within the same region and same capacity tier; fallback to cross-region only if latency SLO allows.
- Eviction interplay: prefetch candidates will be pinned for a short-term TTL (configurable, default 30s) to avoid immediate eviction thrash; eviction ranking will subtract pin weight after TTL expiry.
- Consistency model: eventual consistency acceptable for cached prefixes; however, for pinned prefetch entries that are candidate for function/tool-calling use-cases we will provide a fast invalidation hook via control-plane metadata.
- Instrumentation: must capture per-prefetch hit/miss, prefetch cost (tokens generated for prefetch), and observed latency delta for subsequent requests. These metrics are required before rollout.

Alternatives considered (high level)
- Aggressive ML-based prefetch predictor: higher hit rate in sims but large ops complexity and training/serving cost. Defer to later if heuristics plateau.
- Strict locality-only routing: simplifies consistency but lost flexibility for cost-optimized nodes. Rejected because it increases miss-rate for variable prefixes.
- No-pinning: simpler memory management but observed thrash in July experiments. Rejected.

Experiments & validation plan
- A/B experiment 1 (canary): deploy heuristic + pinning to 5% of traffic (internal load-balanced namespaces) for 2 weeks. Capture: prefetch hit rate, downstream latency improvement, additional token cost per 1k requests, and memory pressure on nodes. Responsible: Marcos Rivera. Start: 2026-08-17.
- Load test: synthetic replay of 48-hour prefix distribution measured from prod traces to confirm eviction behavior under pressure. Responsible: Elena Ivanova. Due: 2026-08-20.
- Observability: add dashboards and alerts (Jordan). Required metrics: prefetch_requests_total, prefetch_hits_total, prefetch_token_cost, prefetch_pinned_entries, prefetch_pin_ttl_evictions, prefetch_fallback_count, latency_before_after_prefetch. Dashboards ready by 2026-08-15.

Rollout & safety controls
- Staged rollout: canary (5%) -> ramp (20%) -> full (100%) with health gates. Health gates: prefetch_miss_rate not increasing > 2% relative, token_cost per request rise < 10% absolute, 95p latency not worse than baseline.
- Kill-switch: routing flag + per-customer prefetch disable. Control-plane flag implement by 2026-08-12.
- Fallback policy: if node's memory pressure > threshold OR prefetch hit-rate < configured min for 10 minutes, disable prefetch on that node for 5 minutes.

Open questions / unresolved items
- How to adjust pin TTL per workload: default 30s works for chat-style workloads but may be too short for long-lived sessions. Need a tuning guide per customer workload type. (Owner: Aisha Patel)
- Cost accounting: should prefetch token generation be billed to customer as part of request or absorbed into platform cost for initial rollout? Finance input needed. (Owner: Priya Singh to loop in finance).
- Deterministic invalidation API: product asks for a synchronous invalidate API for sensitive data. We need security review before exposing. (Owner: Liam Chen)

Action items (owner - due)
- Marcos Rivera: prepare canary deployment plan and experiment definition, include traffic selection and success criteria (2026-08-12)
- Elena Ivanova: run replay load tests and submit report with memory/eviction graphs (2026-08-20)
- Jordan Miles: build dashboards and alert runbook; publish link in Confluence (2026-08-15)
- Aisha Patel: draft tuning guide for pin TTL and per-customer config knobs (2026-08-24)
- Priya Singh: coordinate with finance on prefetch billing recommendation (2026-08-18)
- Liam Chen: prototype control-plane flag for per-customer and global kill-switch (2026-08-12)

Notes from discussion
- July perf experiments: hybrid heuristic produced +18% hit-rate vs baseline and ~6% extra token cost in simulation; memory pressure increased on the largest instance types by ~12% during peak.
- Observability gap called out: no existing metric maps prefetch token cost to customer-level billing; Jordan will add a tag-based aggregation.
- Multi-tenant fairness: suggested per-tenant soft-quota for pinned entries to avoid noisy neighbors - implement as best-effort and enforce via eviction ranking.

Next meeting
- Checkpoint after initial canary metrics are collected (expected 2026-08-31). 30 min sync to review dashboards and decide ramp.

Appendix / references
- RFC: KV Cache Prefetch RFC (link in linked_artifacts)
- GitHub PR: runtime prefetch implementation draft (link in linked_artifacts)
- JIRA: SRV-7890 - tracking canary rollout
